engine_change.reason: The artifact intentionally keeps dense projections and output in source precision. The native-IQ engine previously assumed MMVQ-quantized dense/head tensors and rejected the BF16 pack rows.
behavior: Keep canonical BF16/F32 dense rows when no MMVQ-eligible NativeDense tensor exists.
Keep the canonical BF16 PLE key and output head when those source tensors are not MMVQ types.
Let native-pack prefill and verification use resident BF16 GEMMs for attention/shared projections, with the verifier passing each projection's current F32 input and row stride.
Let the verifier compute the canonical BF16 output head directly.
engine_change.warnings: two pre-existing unused-function/variable warnings; no new build error

non_claims: This is one three-token prompt and eight greedy output tokens, not a quality, KL, NLL, logprob, long-prompt, or coding-evaluation result.
The neutral profile changes cache placement and the GPU hit path rounds differently from the CPU path; the output tokens are not a no-cache correctness oracle.
The throughput numbers are one cold-load run, not interleaved medians or a same-day runtime comparison.
No OpenAI/Anthropic server process, Tetra deployment, multi-GPU run, publication, or Hugging Face upload was exercised.
The source-precision BF16 fallback is functional on this real artifact but not performance-optimized or benchmarked against quantized dense projections.
B550 ctest enumeration could not run because that target-specific build directory did not contain test executables; real SM86 compilation and generation are the backend evidence.
